item.title: Comment on Is it a problem if Wall Street buys up homes? by European Troll
item.description:
> When financial firms buy homes, they also tend to renovate and invest in fixing the places up

It's always good to start your day with a laughter, so this already made my day. What an unqualified statement.

"financial firms" go for most the efficient way to increase earnings and unless Goldman Sachs all of a sudden employs construction managers "fixing places up" is the least efficient one (cash intensive, takes time, produces subjective value) when compared to those that always more lucrative: Just raising the rent, or sell to the current occupants.

Before Goldman Sachs installs new showers they rather split the home into one ore more units.

item.title: Comment on Tuesday assorted links by Tom T.
item.description:
Reply to Welp:

Interesting that most of the progressive state governments pay more to the federal government than they receive.
https://rockinst.org/issue-areas/fiscal-analysis/balance-of-payments-portal/

This is simply false. No state government pays money to the federal government. State governments do not pay any federal taxes.

The geographic incidence of federal tax is simply an indicator of where rich people live. Rich people can vote for progressive state government because they can better afford to insulate themselves from the consequences of doing so.
